correctness.rationale: The exact Jacobian of radial homothety gives boundary cone-density h/(2A) and independent asymptotically uniform radial depth. Four-point nonconvexity has a unique contained point. Its local consecutive-neighbor determinant has the curvature-versus-radial-depth expansion; outside the two-small-gap sector contributions are lower order. In that sector a two-gap product integral gives c/6 using E[(U0-U1)_+]=1/6, and the four-point/six-neighbor combinatorics yields the coefficient A^{-3} integral h^4/kappa ds. Affine invariance follows directly from linear maps; the threefold support-function example is an exact elementary angular integral. Exact algebra and direct planar containment simulations were run from the accompanying checker; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The problem extends the classical Sylvester four-point statistic from a full convex body to a natural vanishing homothetic shell. Its first nontrivial term is not a Taylor term but a δ log(1/δ) singularity from near-neighbor collisions, and its exact coefficient is an affine invariant depending on curvature and support. The circle/ellipse benchmark and explicit nonelliptical support family demonstrate a meaningful shape-sensitive law, not a parameter substitution or tiny numerical improvement.
